skill.name: bio-atac-seq-atac-peak-calling
skill.description: Call accessible chromatin regions from ATAC-seq data using MACS3 with ATAC-specific parameters. Use when identifying open chromatin regions from aligned ATAC-seq BAM files, different from ChIP-seq peak calling.
skill.body:
# ATAC-seq Peak Calling

## Basic MACS3 for ATAC-seq

```bash
# Standard ATAC-seq peak calling
macs3 callpeak \
    -t sample.bam \
    -f BAMPE \
    -g hs \
    -n sample \
    --outdir peaks/ \
    -q 0.05 \
    --nomodel \
    --shift -75 \
    --extsize 150 \
    --keep-dup all \
    -B
```

## Key ATAC-seq Parameters

```bash
# Explained parameters
macs3 callpeak \
    -t sample.bam \        # Treatment BAM
    -f BAMPE \             # Paired-end BAM (uses fragment size)
    -g hs \                # Genome size: hs (human), mm (mouse)
    -n sample \            # Output name prefix
    --nomodel \            # Don't build shifting model
    --shift -75 \          # Shift reads to center on Tn5 cut site
    --extsize 150 \        # Extend reads to this size
    --keep-dup all \       # Keep duplicates (ATAC has natural duplicates)
    -B \                   # Generate bedGraph for visualization
    --call-summits         # Call peak summits
```

## Why These Parameters?

| Parameter | Reason |
|-----------|--------|
| --nomodel | ATAC doesn't have control, can't build model |
| --shift -75 | Centers on Tn5 insertion site |
| --extsize 150 | Smooths signal around cut sites |
| --keep-dup all | Tn5 creates duplicate cuts at accessible sites |
| -f BAMPE | Uses actual fragment size from paired-end |

## Paired-End vs Single-End

```bash
# Paired-end (recommended for ATAC)
macs3 callpeak -f BAMPE -t sample.bam ...

# Single-end (less common)
macs3 callpeak -f BAM -t sample.bam \
    --nomodel --shift -75 --extsize 150 ...
```

## Call Peaks on NFR Only

```bash
# First, filter to nucleosome-free reads (<100bp fragments)
samtools view -h sample.bam | \
    awk 'substr($0,1,1)=="@" || ($9>0 && $9<100) || ($9<0 && $9>-100)' | \
    samtools view -b > nfr.bam

# Call peaks on NFR
macs3 callpeak \
    -t nfr.bam \
    -f BAMPE \
    -g hs \
    -n sample_nfr \
    --nomodel \
    --shift -37 \
    --extsize 75 \
    --keep-dup all \
    -q 0.01
```

## Broad Peaks (Optional)

```bash
# For broader accessible regions
macs3 callpeak \
    -t sample.bam \
    -f BAMPE \
    -g hs \
    -n sample_broad \
    --nomodel \
    --shift -75 \
    --extsize 150 \
    --broad \
    --broad-cutoff 0.1
```

## Batch Processing

```bash
#!/bin/bash
GENOME=hs  # hs for human, mm for mouse
OUTDIR=peaks

mkdir -p $OUTDIR

for bam in *.bam; do
    sample=$(basename $bam .bam)
    echo "Processing $sample..."

    macs3 callpeak \
        -t $bam \
        -f BAMPE \
        -g $GENOME \
        -n $sample \
        --outdir $OUTDIR \
        --nomodel \
        --shift -75 \
        --extsize 150 \
        --keep-dup all \
        -q 0.05 \
        -B \
        --call-summits
done
```

## Output Files

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| _peaks.narrowPeak | Peak locations (BED-like) |
| _summits.bed | Peak summit positions |
| _peaks.xls | Peak statistics (Excel format) |
| _treat_pileup.bdg | Signal track (bedGraph) |
| _control_lambda.bdg | Background (if control provided) |

## narrowPeak Format

```
chr1  100  500  peak1  500  .  10.5  50.2  45.1  200
```

Columns: chrom, start, end, name, score, strand, signalValue, pValue, qValue, summit_offset

## Convert to BigWig

```bash
# Sort bedGraph
sort -k1,1 -k2,2n sample_treat_pileup.bdg > sample.sorted.bdg

# Convert to BigWig
bedGraphToBigWig sample.sorted.bdg chrom.sizes sample.bw
```

## Merge Replicates

```bash
# Pool BAMs before peak calling (recommended for final peaks)
samtools merge -@ 8 merged.bam rep1.bam rep2.bam rep3.bam

# Call peaks on merged
macs3 callpeak -t merged.bam -f BAMPE -g hs -n merged ...
```

## IDR for Replicate Consistency

```bash
# Call peaks on each replicate
macs3 callpeak -t rep1.bam -f BAMPE -g hs -n rep1 ...
macs3 callpeak -t rep2.bam -f BAMPE -g hs -n rep2 ...

# Run IDR
idr --samples rep1_peaks.narrowPeak rep2_peaks.narrowPeak \
    --input-file-type narrowPeak \
    --output-file idr_peaks.txt \
    --plot

# Filter by IDR threshold
awk '$5 >= 540' idr_peaks.txt > reproducible_peaks.bed
```

generated_query: I have a set of paired-end BAM files from human ATAC-seq experiments on T cells. I need to call accessible chromatin regions (open chromatin peaks) using MACS3 with the appropriate ATAC-seq parameters. Specifically, I want to use the Tn5 shift correction (--shift -75, --extsize 150), keep duplicates (--keep-dup all), and output both narrowPeak files and signal bedGraph tracks for each sample. I also need to convert the bedGraph to bigWig for genome browser viewing. Could you help me write the command line for processing one sample (sample.bam) and explain the key parameters? After that, I have three replicates that I plan to merge before peak calling – can you show how to pool the BAMs and then run MACS3 on the merged file? Finally, I want to assess reproducibility using IDR between two replicates – please provide the steps to call peaks on individual replicates and then run IDR.

edit_instructions.target_text:
## IDR for Replicate Consistency

```bash
# Call peaks on each replicate
macs3 callpeak -t rep1.bam -f BAMPE -g hs -n rep1 ...
macs3 callpeak -t rep2.bam -f BAMPE -g hs -n rep2 ...

# Run IDR
idr --samples rep1_peaks.narrowPeak rep2_peaks.narrowPeak \
    --input-file-type narrowPeak \
    --output-file idr_peaks.txt \
    --plot

# Filter by IDR threshold
awk '$5 >= 540' idr_peaks.txt > reproducible_peaks.bed
```

# ATAC-seq Peak Calling with MACS3

## Basic MACS3 for ATAC-seq

```bash
# Standard ATAC-seq peak calling (single-end mode)
macs3 callpeak \
    -t sample.bam \
    -f BAM \               # Treat as single-end (even if paired-end data)
    -g hs \                # Human genome
    -n sample \
    --outdir peaks/ \
    -q 0.05 \
    --nomodel \
    --shift -75 \          # Tn5 shift for single-end
    --extsize 150 \        # Extension length
    -B                     # Generate bedGraph
```

## Key Parameters Explained

| Parameter | Value | Purpose |
|-----------|-------|---------|
| `-f BAM` | Single-end | Forces single-end processing regardless of input format |
| `--nomodel` | – | Skips model building (no control needed) |
| `--shift -75` | -75 | Adjusts reads to Tn5 cut site (single-end convention) |
| `--extsize 150` | 150 | Smooths signal around cut sites |
| `-q 0.05` | 0.05 | q-value cutoff for peak significance |

> **Note:** For paired-end data, use `-f BAMPE` instead and omit `--shift`/`--extsize`. However, the single-end approach with these adjustment parameters is also commonly used.

## Batch Processing

```bash
#!/bin/bash
GENOME=mm   # Mouse genome (change to hs for human)
OUTDIR=peaks
mkdir -p $OUTDIR

for bam in *.bam; do
    sample=$(basename $bam .bam)
    macs3 callpeak \
        -t $bam \
        -f BAM \
        -g $GENOME \
        -n $sample \
        --outdir $OUTDIR \
        --nomodel \
        --shift -75 \
        --extsize 150 \
        -q 0.05 \
        -B
done
```

## Output Files

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `_peaks.narrowPeak` | Peak regions |
| `_summits.bed` | Peak summits |
| `_treat_pileup.bdg` | Signal bedGraph |
| `_peaks.xls` | Peak statistics |

## Merge Replicates (Simple Pooling)

```bash
# Merge BAMs by concatenation (requires sorted and indexed inputs)
samtools cat -o merged.bam rep1.bam rep2.bam rep3.bam

# Index merged BAM

# Filter by IDR score (use column 5 as signal value)
awk '$5 >= 500' idr_peaks.txt > reproducible_peaks.bed
```

## Additional Tips

- For nucleosome-free analysis, filter fragments < 100 bp before peak calling.
- Use `--broad` for broader accessible regions (optional).
- Always verify genome sizes with `-g` (hs for human, mm for mouse).

# ATAC-seq Peak Calling

## Basic MACS3 for ATAC-seq

```bash
# Standard ATAC-seq peak calling
macs3 callpeak \
    -t sample.bam \
    -f BAMPE \
    -g hs \
    -n sample \
    --outdir peaks/ \
    -q 0.05 \
    --nomodel \
    --shift -75 \
    --extsize 150 \
    --keep-dup all \

```

## Key ATAC-seq Parameters

```bash
# Explained parameters
macs3 callpeak \
    -t sample.bam \        # Treatment BAM
    -f BAMPE \             # Paired-end BAM (uses fragment size)
    -g hs \                # Genome size: hs (human), mm (mouse)
    -n sample \            # Output name prefix
    --nomodel \            # Don't build shifting model
    --shift -75 \          # Shift reads to center on Tn5 cut site
    --extsize 150 \        # Extend reads to this size
    --keep-dup all \       # Keep duplicates (ATAC has natural duplicates)
    -B \                   # Generate bedGraph for visualization
    --call-summits         # Call peak summits
```

## Why These Parameters?

| Parameter | Reason |
|-----------|--------|
| --nomodel | ATAC doesn't have control, can't build model |
| --shift -75 | Centers on Tn5 insertion site |
| --extsize 150 | Smooths signal around cut sites |
| --keep-dup all | Tn5 creates duplicate cuts at accessible sites |
| -f BAMPE | Uses actual fragment size from paired-end |

## Paired-End vs Single-End

```bash
# Paired-end (recommended for ATAC)
macs3 callpeak -f BAMPE -t sample.bam ...

# Single-end (less common)
macs3 callpeak -f BAM -t sample.bam \
    --nomodel --shift -75 --extsize 150 ...
```

## Call Peaks on NFR Only

```bash
# First, filter to nucleosome-free reads (<100bp fragments)
samtools view -h sample.bam | \
    awk 'substr($0,1,1)=="@" || ($9>0 && $9<100) || ($9<0 && $9>-100)' | \
    samtools view -b > nfr.bam

# Call peaks on NFR
macs3 callpeak \
    -t nfr.bam \
    -f BAMPE \
    -g hs \
    -n sample_nfr \
    --nomodel \
    --shift -37 \
    --extsize 75 \
    --keep-dup all \
    -q 0.01
```

## Broad Peaks (Optional)

```bash
# For broader accessible regions
macs3 callpeak \
    -t sample.bam \
    -f BAMPE \
    -g hs \
    -n sample_broad \
    --nomodel \
    --shift -75 \
    --extsize 150 \
    --broad \
    --broad-cutoff 0.1
```

## Batch Processing

```bash
#!/bin/bash
GENOME=hs  # hs for human, mm for mouse
OUTDIR=peaks

mkdir -p $OUTDIR

for bam in *.bam; do
    sample=$(basename $bam .bam)
    echo "Processing $sample..."

    macs3 callpeak \
        -t $bam \
        -f BAMPE \
        -g $GENOME \
        -n $sample \
        --outdir $OUTDIR \
        --nomodel \
        --shift -75 \
        --extsize 150 \
        --keep-dup all \
        -q 0.05 \
        -B \
        --call-summits
done
```

## Output Files

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| _peaks.narrowPeak | Peak locations (BED-like) |
| _summits.bed | Peak summit positions |
| _peaks.xls | Peak statistics (Excel format) |
| _treat_pileup.bdg | Signal track (bedGraph) |
| _control_lambda.bdg | Background (if control provided) |

## narrowPeak Format

```
chr1  100  500  peak1  500  .  10.5  50.2  45.1  200
```

Columns: chrom, start, end, name, score, strand, signalValue, pValue, qValue, summit_offset

## Convert to BigWig

```bash
# Sort bedGraph
sort -k1,1 -k2,2n sample_treat_pileup.bdg > sample.sorted.bdg

# Convert to BigWig
bedGraphToBigWig sample.sorted.bdg chrom.sizes sample.bw
```

## Merge Replicates

```bash
# Pool BAMs before peak calling (recommended for final peaks)
samtools merge -@ 8 merged.bam rep1.bam rep2.bam rep3.bam

# Call peaks on merged
macs3 callpeak -t merged.bam -f BAMPE -g hs -n merged ...
```

## IDR for Replicate Consistency

```bash
# Call peaks on each replicate
macs3 callpeak -t rep1.bam -f BAMPE -g hs -n rep1 ...
macs3 callpeak -t rep2.bam -f BAMPE -g hs -n rep2 ...

# Run IDR
idr --samples rep1_peaks.narrowPeak rep2_peaks.narrowPeak \
    --input-file-type narrowPeak \
    --output-file idr_peaks.txt \
    --plot

# Filter by IDR threshold
awk '$5 >= 540' idr_peaks.txt > reproducible_peaks.bed
```
